## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design multi-tenant upgrade workflows with strict rollback mechanisms and metric-driven canary promotion—a common production CNF pattern at scale.

## Key Concepts
- Canary deployments per-tenant using Istio or Linkerd for traffic splitting
- TenantUpgradePolicy CRD design for declarative upgrade management
- Metric-driven promotion windows with Prometheus and SLO definitions
- Safe rollback capabilities with idempotent manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantUpgradePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-upgrade
spec:
  tenantId: tenant-a
  targetVersion: v2.1.0
  canaryTrafficPercent: 5
  promotionCriteria:
    latencyThresholdMs: 100
    errorRateThresholdPercent: 0.5
    observationWindowMinutes: 10
  rollbackConfig:
    autoRollbackOnFailure: true
    maxRetries: 3
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:

```

## Why This Is Asked

- Kubernetes CertificateSigningRequest flow
- Per-namespace per-tenant CA

```yaml
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
```

Why This Is Asked
- Tests cross-cluster policy propagation, conflict handling, and secure identity management
- Validates runtime enforcement by per-tenant sidecars in a multi-cluster CNF gateway mesh
- Probes reconciliation loops and secure communication patterns

Key Concepts
- CustomResourceDefinition for TenantPolicy
- Cross-cluster replication with mTLS and SPIFFE IDs
- Dynamic gateway policy loading in sidecars
- Conflict resolution and eventual consistency

Code Example
```yaml
# CRD: TenantPolicy
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantpolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID:
                type: string
              namespaces:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
              rules:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    action:
                      type: string
                      enum: [allow, deny]
                    resources:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: tenantpolicies
    singular: tenantpolicy
    kind: TenantPolicy
```

```yaml
# Policy Agent Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: policy-agent
  namespace: cnf-system
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: policy-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: policy-agent
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: agent
        image: policy-agent:latest
        env:
        - name: REMOTE_CLUSTER
          value: "peer-cluster.example.com"
        - name: SPIFFE_TRUST_DOMAIN
          value: "example.com"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: spiffe-bundle
          mountPath: /run/spiffe
      volumes:
      - name: spiffe-bundle
        configMap:
          name: spiffe-bundle
```

```yaml
spec:
  tenantID: tenant-a
  namespaces:
  - tenant-a

  - action: allow
    resources:
    - service-a
    - service-b
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime attestation bridging CI and runtime, using SPIFFE/mTLS, OPA, and per-tenant revocation. Evaluates trade-offs around performance, key management, and revocation latency.

## Key Concepts

- Runtime attestation evidence (image digest, SBOM hash, runtime state)
- Attestation service with mutual TLS and SPIFFE identities
- Admission control with OPA to gate scheduling
- Per-tenant revocation and key rotation for attestations
- Testing in a single namespace before broader rollout

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: attestation-agent
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: agent
        image: example/attestation-agent:latest
        env:
        - name: ATTESTATION_ENDPOINT
          value: https://attestor.default.svc.cluster.local
        - name: CERT_FILE
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: attestation-cert
              key: tls.crt
        - name: KEY_FILE
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: attestation-cert
              key: tls.key
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you scale attestation for thousands of CNFs without adding startup latency?
- How would you handle revocation propagation when an attacker signs a new image at runtime?

## Why This Is Asked

This tests end-to-end upgrade governance at scale: enforcing tenant isolation, cross-cluster canaries, and SBOM-based gates in production.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-cluster Argo Rollouts canary strategies
- OPA/Kyverno style policies for time-window upgrades
- SBOM integrity checks as upgrade gates
- Tenant isolation via SPIFFE IDs
- Central audit webhook for traceability

## Code Example
```yaml
# Argo Rollouts canary manifest (minimal)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-rollout
spec:
  replicas: 2
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: cnf
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 300s }
```

```yaml
# Audit webhook payload (example)
tenant: tenant-A
upgrade: cnf-service:1.2.3
cluster: eu-west-1
status: canary
```
